# Asclepius

> Connected care, explained: a browser-only educational demo for healthcare stakeholders exploring synthetic workflows, with a separate local TypeScript/FHIR teaching core.

NOT_FOR_CLINICAL_USE. Fictional examples only. Do not use real patient data or interpret validation as clinical safety or full FHIR conformance. The local drug-interaction knowledge base is intentionally incomplete.

Two cases, each with nine records: Alex Morgan's routine follow-up and Maya Chen's referral from Willow to Cedar. In Maya's fixed snapshot the referral is active, coordination is completed, and the receiving visit is planned. Navigating stages does not send referrals or change care status. The browser demo makes no API calls and needs no account.

## Explore

- [Referral review](https://safetymp.github.io/Asclepius/): compare a synthetic report with its request, make a queue decision and weigh an onboarding pilot.
- [Technical workspace](https://safetymp.github.io/Asclepius/workspace/): a compact guide to the tools and fixture limits.
- [Care journeys](https://safetymp.github.io/Asclepius/journeys/): switch between both cases and follow the stages.
- [Resource explorer](https://safetymp.github.io/Asclepius/resources/): inspect synthetic records and their connections.
- [Validation lab](https://safetymp.github.io/Asclepius/validate/): eleven hand-authored schemas and three teaching rules, checked locally.
- [How it works](https://safetymp.github.io/Asclepius/architecture/): stakeholder context and developer architecture.
- [Sitemap](https://safetymp.github.io/Asclepius/sitemap.xml): canonical public pages.
